neighbours.label: the quantifier or ordinal right before a song or poem section ('the first [verse]', 'each [stanza]', 'three [parts]'), predicting the section word
fire: The singer changes the melody slightly at the end of each verse of the ballad.
In the first verse she sings about leaving her home town behind.
The poem repeats the same line at the close of every stanza.
The band plays the hook twice before the second chorus comes in.
This reel is usually played in two parts, with the high part repeated.
The hymn has four verses, and the congregation stands for the last one.
The guitarist takes a short solo after the third chorus of the song.
Each line of the sonnet's final couplet rhymes with the other.
quiet: The tour guide changes the route slightly at the end of each day of the trip.
In the first week she studies the history of her home town.
The lawyer repeats the same point at the close of every hearing.
The team runs the drill twice before the second half begins.
This road is usually built in two parts, with the steep part paved.
The house has four bedrooms, and the guests stay in the last one.
The goalkeeper made a short run after the third corner of the game.
Each line of the shopping list was crossed off by the evening.

notes: Card: peaks on ' first' x5, ' each' x2, ' three' x2 in music/poetry structure text (first two lines, end of each stanza, in three parts, each of the last four verses). Logit: + pole suppresses ' verse', ' chorus', ' bridge', ' stanza'-like words, so the - pole predicts them. Near misses keep the quantifier but in non-music contexts of the same length.
